chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muskhan, from Isma'il ibn Jabir, from Abu Basir, and from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Basir, and 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Yunus ibn 'Abdyan, all of them from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
A mandatory prayer is superior to twenty pilgrimages, and a pilgrimage is better than a house of gold given in charity until nothing of it remains.
ai.seo_question: What is the comparative reward of an obligatory prayer versus the Hajj pilgrimage in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines a spiritual hierarchy where the consistent observance of the obligatory prayer (Salat) outweighs the cumulative merit of twenty Hajj pilgrimages, emphasizing the primacy of daily devotion. He further elevates the status of a single Hajj above the complete expenditure of a gold house in charity, highlighting the unique, multi-dimensional spiritual benefits of the pilgrimage. This comparison reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the foundational role of Salat as the pillar of Islam, while still recognizing Hajj as a supreme act of worship and purification.
